# Product Software Engineer I — Disney Entertainment and ESPN Product & Technology

---

**Job ID:** 10151599
**Date Posted:** Aug 12, 2026
**Date Applied:** Aug 14, 2026
**Salary Range:** $97,500 – $130,700 / year (Glendale, CA hiring range, 40-hour week)

---

## Job Summary

An entry-level engineering role on Disney's Ad Platforms team (Disney Entertainment and ESPN Product & Technology), building and supporting software behind Disney's advertising-technology products — data processing and platform applications — while learning modern engineering practices, cloud/big-data tooling, and AI-assisted development under senior-engineer guidance. Primarily on-site, Glendale, CA.

---

## What You'll Do

- Develop and maintain software components for data-processing and platform applications; assist building batch and near-real-time data pipelines with senior-engineer guidance.
- Write clean, readable, testable code; use AI-assisted development tools for coding, debugging, testing, and documentation.
- Participate in design discussions, implementation, testing, troubleshooting, and code review.
- Learn and apply cloud technologies and big-data frameworks; support production systems and help investigate technical issues.

### Required Qualifications
- 0–2 years of software development experience (internships, academic projects, or equivalent hands-on experience count)
- Foundational experience with a language such as Java, Scala, or Python
- Understanding of data-processing concepts and interest in learning big-data tools (Spark, Kafka, Flink, Databricks, Snowflake)
- Basic SQL/relational-database knowledge; familiarity with cloud concepts (AWS, Terraform, Docker, Kubernetes) an interest, not a requirement
- Curiosity, adaptability, and strong communication skills

### Education
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Software, Electrical or Electronics Engineering, or a comparable field of study, or equivalent work experience.

### Benefits
Standard Disney benefits package; bonus and/or long-term incentive units depending on level; full range of medical/financial benefits.

---

## How I Match Up

### At Application — Aug 14, 2026

- **Partial overlap:** Python is an explicit skill, and a BS in Electro-Mechanical Engineering plausibly satisfies "a comparable field of study."
- **The honest headline for this one is a level mismatch, not a skills mismatch:** this is a Level I / 0–2-year entry role, while the application here represents roughly 6 years of professional engineering experience, including CTO-level and Lead R&D Engineer responsibilities. That's the opposite direction of most gaps in this tracker — overqualified on seniority rather than underqualified on skill.
- **Genuine skill gaps too:** no Java or Scala evidence, and no SQL/relational-database or big-data (Spark/Kafka/Databricks/Snowflake) experience on record — the actual data-engineering stack this role uses.
- The tracker shows this one moved to "No longer in consideration" on Aug 20, 2026, six days after applying — consistent with the level mismatch above.

### Now — Aug 22, 2026

No material change — nothing Java/Scala/SQL/big-data-specific has been added since application, and this application is already closed.

---

## About the Company

This posting sits under Disney Entertainment and ESPN Product & Technology's Ad Platforms team, responsible for Disney's ad technology and products across its sports, news, and entertainment content.
